complaint.name: Synthetic Customer 041
complaint.title: [DEMO C041] Airtable authentication links fail for late arrivals
complaint.description: Older Airtable connection links show expiry errors for returning users, while fresh connections work, reducing onboarding completion.

hypotheses.description: Most likely cause for the observed failed Airtable auth execution is an expired authentication initiation. The canonical failed request was already older than its 600s completion window, returned EXPIRED/410, and never attempted provider token exchange. A controlled sandbox comparison shows the same age-related condition fails while a fresh initiation succeeds.
assumptions: The observed cedar request is representative of the reported older-link failures.
The controlled comparison validates initiation age as the discriminating factor for this flow, though not every possible production path is directly observed.

hypotheses.description: OAuth redirect URI mismatch is a weaker alternative. Current evidence does not show a callback/config mismatch; instead the observed request is marked EXPIRED before any token exchange, and freshness alone flips the outcome in the controlled comparison.
assumptions: Direct callback/configuration records are not present, so this alternative is not fully ruled out.

hypotheses.description: An internal contributing change outside tool-executor remains unconfirmed. There is no observed tool-executor deployment in the incident window, but missing auth-service or session-policy change telemetry means an upstream policy or TTL change cannot be excluded as a deeper reason why expiries were prevalent.
assumptions: Any internal contributor would more likely sit in auth-service or session-policy than in a new tool-executor release.
Absence of a tool-executor deployment does not prove no dependency-side change occurred.

recommended_actions: Use a fresh Airtable authentication initiation for affected users and avoid retrying expired links; recommended actions have not been executed.
Collect canonical auth-flow telemetry that links initiation creation time, callback receipt, expiry decision, and any dependency policy outcome for affected attempts.
Align synthetic telemetry across auth-flow and executor stages so old-link failures and fresh-link successes can be counted by initiation age.
If redirect mismatch is still suspected, verify canonical OAuth callback/config records for the affected Airtable flow.
Collect auth-service and session-policy deployment/config history for the incident window, especially TTL, clock, and callback-expiry handling.
limitations: Synthetic telemetry is incomplete: metrics required a retry after timeout, and there are no canonical initiation-creation or callback-series records for the broader population.
The maple success log is a healthy same-provider comparison, but not direct production proof of fresh auth-link success; the stronger freshness control is the sandbox comparison.
History evidence is analogy only and not proof of the current cause.
Observed evidence diagnoses the failed execution and localized impact, but does not fully establish why many cedar attempts were in expired state.

findings.statement: A canonical production Airtable auth request failed with 410 EXPIRED at initiation_age_seconds=950 against completion_window_seconds=600, and token exchange was not attempted.

In the controlled comparison, the aged initiation at 950s failed with 410 EXPIRED and no token exchange, while the otherwise matched fresh initiation at 120s succeeded with ACTIVE state and token exchange attempted.
The observed failed request did not reach provider token exchange, so provider-side Airtable failure is a weaker explanation for this execution.
Observed evidence weakens a provider-wide outage explanation: provider_api_reachable=true, and a same-time comparison tenant had a successful same-provider operation.

Impact is substantial but localized. Cedar had 636 requests with 390 failures and 390 blocked operations, queue depth 114, and p95 latency 1520ms, while maple had 538 requests with 0 failures, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160ms.

The affected tenant also showed elevated queue depth and latency during the window, but the observed failed request was already past its completion window, so backlog is observed context rather than the demonstrated immediate mechanism.
No tool-executor deployment was observed in the incident window, and the only deployment found overall was an unrelated support-dashboard release.

Tool-executor depends on auth-service, provider-api, and session-policy, so dependency-side policy or TTL behavior could still matter even though the immediate observed mechanism is expired initiation.

Important causal coverage is missing because canonical initiation-creation, callback-series, and dependency change records are not present for the broader population of reported old-link and fresh-link attempts.
